note.explanation: Air molecules move randomly and collide with objects. These collisions exert force over an area, creating atmospheric pressure. This pressure acts in all directions and decreases as altitude increases.
examples: At sea level, atmospheric pressure is about 1.013 × 10⁵ Pa.
When steam in a closed tin can cools and condenses, the outside atmospheric pressure can crush the can.
note.checkAnswer: Atmospheric pressure decreases as altitude increases.
note.simple: Air presses on us from every direction. The higher you go, the less air is above you, so the pressure is lower.
note.checkQuestion: What happens to atmospheric pressure as altitude increases?
note.title: Atmospheric Pressure
steps: Remember: pressure is force per unit area.
Air molecules collide with objects and exert force.
The force per unit area caused by the atmosphere is atmospheric pressure.
Atmospheric pressure is greatest at sea level and decreases with altitude.
note.answer: Atmospheric pressure is the force per unit area exerted by the atmosphere.

options: The force per unit area exerted by the atmosphere
The total weight of the atmosphere
The force exerted only downward by air
The pressure inside a sealed container
rationales: This is correct because atmospheric pressure is the force per unit area exerted by the atmosphere.
This is incorrect because atmospheric pressure describes force per unit area, not the atmosphere’s total weight.
This is incorrect because atmospheric pressure acts in all directions, not only downward.
This is incorrect because pressure inside a container is not necessarily atmospheric pressure.

options: Only in the direction of the wind
mcqs.stem: In which directions does atmospheric pressure act?
rationales: This is incorrect because random molecular motion does not produce pressure only upward.
This is incorrect because atmospheric pressure is not limited to the downward direction.
This is correct because air molecules move randomly, so atmospheric pressure acts equally in all directions.
This is incorrect because pressure is not restricted to the direction of the wind.

mcqs.stem: How does atmospheric pressure change as altitude increases?
rationales: This is incorrect because the section states that atmospheric pressure decreases with height.
This is correct because atmospheric pressure falls as we go higher in the air.
This is incorrect because atmospheric pressure does not remain constant with altitude.
This is incorrect because the section gives a pressure of 55 kPa at about 5 km, not zero.

mcqs.stem: What is the approximate standard atmospheric pressure at sea level?
rationales: This is correct because the section gives standard atmospheric pressure as about 1.013 × 10⁵ Pa.
This is incorrect because it is much smaller than the stated sea-level pressure.
This is incorrect because it is much larger than the stated sea-level pressure.
This is incorrect because it is far below the stated sea-level pressure.

options: The air inside the can pushes harder than the outside air
Cooling steam reduces the pressure inside, so outside atmospheric pressure crushes the can
Cold water adds enough weight to flatten the can
The can loses all its metal strength when heated
mcqs.stem: Why does a tin can crumple after steam inside it condenses?
rationales: This is incorrect because condensing steam lowers, rather than increases, the pressure inside the can.
This is correct because the lower inside pressure allows the greater outside atmospheric pressure to crumple the can.
This is incorrect because the activity explains the crushing through atmospheric pressure, not the water’s weight.
This is incorrect because the can is crumpled by the pressure difference, not because it loses all strength.

options: It changes direction but not value
mcqs.stem: What happens to atmospheric pressure when a point is moved from sea level to a greater altitude?
rationales: This is incorrect because atmospheric pressure falls with increasing altitude.
This is correct because the section states that pressure decreases as we go up in the air.
This is incorrect because atmospheric pressure varies with altitude.
This is incorrect because the pressure’s value decreases; it is not merely a change in direction.

written.text: Q6.9. What is the basic principle to measure the atmospheric pressure by a simple mercury barometer?
written.finalAnswer: The atmospheric pressure is balanced by the pressure due to the mercury column.

rubric.why: The answer must identify what pressure is being measured and what balances it.
rubric.description: Identify atmospheric pressure and the mercury column.
rubric.how: State that the mercury column balances the atmospheric pressure.

rubric.why: The balancing principle is the basic working principle of the barometer.
rubric.how: Explain that the pressure exerted by the mercury column balances atmospheric pressure.

modelAnswer: In a simple mercury barometer, atmospheric pressure is balanced by the pressure due to the mercury column.
The height of the mercury column indicates the atmospheric pressure.

written.text: Q6.6. If some air remains trapped within the top of the mercury column of the barometer which is supposed to be vacuum, how would it affect the height of the mercury column?
written.finalAnswer: The mercury column would be lower than its correct height.

rubric.why: The answer must give the direction of the change in the column height.
rubric.description: State the effect on the mercury height.
rubric.how: Say that the mercury column would be lower.

rubric.why: The explanation must connect the trapped air’s pressure to the reduced height.
rubric.how: State that trapped air exerts pressure at the top of the mercury column, so the column is lower than its correct height.

modelAnswer: Trapped air at the top of the mercury column would exert pressure on the mercury.
Therefore, the mercury column would be lower than its correct height.

written.text: Q6.8. The end of glass tube used in a simple barometer is not properly sealed, some leak is present. What will be its effect?
written.finalAnswer: Air entering through the leak would make the mercury column lower than its correct height.

rubric.why: The answer must identify what enters through the faulty seal.
rubric.description: Identify the effect of the leak in the tube.
rubric.how: State that air can enter the tube through the leak.

rubric.why: The answer must explain how the leak affects the barometer reading.
rubric.description: State the effect on the column.
rubric.how: Explain that air pressure in the tube makes the mercury column lower than its correct height.

modelAnswer: Air would enter through the leak and exert pressure above the mercury column.
The mercury column would be lower than its correct height, so the barometer reading would be incorrect.

written.text: Q6.5. Explain that atmosphere exerts pressure. What are its applications? Give at least three examples.
written.finalAnswer: Air molecules collide with objects and exert force per unit area; atmospheric pressure acts in all directions and can be measured with a barometer, used to estimate altitude, and demonstrated by a crumpling can.

rubric.why: This explains how the atmosphere produces pressure.
rubric.description: Explain the cause of atmospheric pressure.
rubric.how: Describe air molecules colliding with objects and exerting force per unit area.

rubric.why: The section specifically states that atmospheric pressure acts equally in all directions.
rubric.description: State the direction of atmospheric pressure.
rubric.how: Mention that it acts equally in all directions.

rubric.why: A barometer is an example of measuring atmospheric pressure.
rubric.how: Name a barometer as a way to measure atmospheric pressure.

rubric.why: Further examples show the use or evidence of atmospheric pressure.
rubric.how: Mention using pressure to determine altitude and/or the can-crumpling activity as evidence.

modelAnswer: Air molecules are always in motion and collide with objects, exerting force on them.
This force per unit area is atmospheric pressure, and it acts equally in all directions.
Atmospheric pressure can be used to determine altitude; the can-crumpling activity also demonstrates its effect.

written.text: Q6.6. What will be the height of the column in barometer at sea level if mercury is replaced by water of density 1000 kg m⁻³, where density of mercury is 13.6 × 10³ kg m⁻³

rubric.why: Using the pressure relation for a fluid column sets up the barometer calculation.
rubric.how: Use P = ρgh for the mercury and water columns.

rubric.why: The same atmospheric pressure is balanced by either fluid column.
rubric.how: Set the mercury-column pressure equal to the water-column pressure and use the given densities.

rubric.why: Correct substitution and calculation lead to the height before rounding.
rubric.how: Use the sea-level mercury height of about 0.76 m and calculate the equivalent water height.

rubric.why: The final result must agree with the textbook answer.
rubric.description: Give the final answer with unit.
rubric.how: Round the calculated height to 10.3 m.

modelAnswer: At sea level, atmospheric pressure = pressure due to the mercury column.
ρmercury g hmercury = ρwater g hwater

For explanation questions, link air molecules’ collisions to force per unit area; include the all-directions point when relevant.
In a barometer question, state that atmospheric pressure is balanced by the pressure due to the mercury column.
For the water-barometer numerical, equate ρgh for mercury and water, cancel g, show the substitution, and write the final unit.

steps.why: Heating the water produces steam that fills the tin can.
steps.text: Boil some water in a tin can until it is full of steam.

steps.why: Closing the can limits the entry of outside air.
steps.text: Remove the can from the burner and close its mouth with an air-tight cork.

steps.why: Cold water cools the steam so that it condenses.
steps.text: Pour cold water over the can.

steps.why: Condensation lowers the pressure inside, so the greater outside atmospheric pressure crushes the can.
steps.text: The can crumples because the atmospheric pressure outside presses in more strongly than the pressure inside.

example.question: ACTIVITY 6.5: Boil some water in a tin can. When it is full of steam, remove it from the burner and close its mouth by an air tight cork. Then pour cold water over it. The can crumples as shown in the figure. Why does the tin crumples?
example.answer: The steam condenses when cooled, lowering the pressure inside the can. The greater atmospheric pressure outside crushes it.

explain.title: What atmospheric pressure means
explain.body: The Earth is surrounded by air called the atmosphere. Air molecules move and collide with objects. Your textbook defines it this way: “This force per unit area is the atmospheric pressure.”

explain.title: Pressure acts in all directions
explain.body: Air molecules move randomly and collide with objects from different directions. Your textbook states: “Since the molecules of air have random motion, therefore, atmospheric pressure acts equally in all directions.”

explain.title: Pressure at sea level
explain.body: At sea level, atmospheric pressure is about 1.013 × 10⁵ Pa. Your textbook calls this value standard atmospheric pressure.

explain.title: Atmospheric pressure changes with height
explain.body: Air density decreases with altitude, and atmospheric pressure decreases as we go higher. Your textbook gives about 55 kPa at 5 km and 1 kPa at 30 km. Lower atmospheric pressure means greater altitude.

explain.title: Evidence of atmospheric pressure
explain.body: In the tin-can activity, steam condenses as the can cools. The pressure inside falls, and the outside atmospheric pressure pushes the can inward.

mistakes: Do not say atmospheric pressure acts only downward; it acts equally in all directions.
Do not confuse pressure with force: pressure is force per unit area.
Do not say atmospheric pressure increases with altitude; it decreases as altitude increases.
In the can activity, explain the pressure difference: cooling lowers the pressure inside and outside atmospheric pressure crushes the can.
In the water-barometer calculation, do not forget to use the same pressure for both columns and include the final unit.
